statement: Let P=SW2 with the face numbering and reflective chamber tiling of Allcock--Devlin--Felikson--Kontorovich--Whitehead, arXiv:2609.05349v1. If Q is a convex finite-volume ideal right-angled P-polyhedron consisting of at most 84 SW2 chambers, then Q consists of exactly 48 SW2 chambers and is isometric to the ideal right-angled hyperbolic octahedron O. In particular, Q is tiled by one copy of O. This statement makes no assertion for P-polyhedra with more than 84 chambers, and the original Conjecture 7.11 remains unresolved.
contribution: An exact exhaustive finite classification through seven quarter-octahedron volume units, covering both canonical face-type branches in Proposition 7.10. It adds a certified local-block enumeration, an exact convexity obstruction for every rejected interface mismatch, complete symmetry-class enumeration, and Lorentz-Gram isometry certificates for the survivors. It rules out counterexamples through 84 SW2 chambers but does not claim an unbounded result or priority beyond the documented limited literature screen.
